title: Micro-Timescale Human Admissibility
claim: Human conversation can implement a continuously evaluated admissibility gate at the shortest practical human-human interaction timescale.

variables.I: speaker intended referent or communicative goal
variables.u_n: candidate utterance at repair step n
variables.q_n: listener confidence that reconstructed referent matches intent
variables.qhat_n: speaker estimate of listener reconstruction confidence

equations.listener_confidence: q_n = P(r_n = I | u_n, x_n, E_1:n)
equations.candidate_update: u_(n+1) = u_n + Delta(I, u_n, f_n, x_n)
equations.mutually_observable_crossing_time: t_M = inf{t : q(t) >= tau_A and qhat(t) >= tau_A}
equations.commitment_time: t_C = inf{t >= t_M : q(t) >= tau_C and a(t) != 0}

gate_question: Has the intended referent been reconstructed with sufficient current evidence and standing for consequential response to begin?

receipt.boundary: receipt of understanding is not proof of objective truth or unrestricted authority

research_hypotheses.name: incremental_correction
research_hypotheses.claim: Successive child utterances in unresolved interactions show non-random acoustic variation correlated with caregiver feedback.

research_hypotheses.name: feedback_sensitive_termination
research_hypotheses.claim: Repetition terminates more strongly after referent-consistent caregiver action than after generic acknowledgment.

research_hypotheses.name: evidence_accumulation
research_hypotheses.claim: Listener accuracy depends on prior attempts and not only on the final utterance.

research_hypotheses.name: mutual_observability
research_hypotheses.claim: Speaker termination is predicted by visible and prosodic evidence of listener understanding.

research_hypotheses.name: timescale_compression
research_hypotheses.claim: Development preserves the repair loop while shifting it from overt repetition toward faster substitution, prosodic adjustment, and internal prediction.
